criteria.evidence: "A person gives one web-page file, which is a file whose name ends in .html or .htm." "Given a path with no file, when the capture runs, then it fails and the record names the path." "A project with many files. Specify from a project folder (fn-specify-from-folder) does this."

"The browser does not follow mail, phone or script links, or any link that starts with http or https. It follows relative links." "The size limit is 40 views beyond the first screen, or 160 clicks." "A named control is clicked with no word test. A named control that cannot be found fails the capture."
criteria.fix: Give the reason beside each of these three rules, so a reader does not have to guess. Links: say why mail, phone, script and http or https links are not followed (they lead out of the prototype, so the capture stays inside the one file and its relative links). Size limit: say why there is a cap (so a prototype with endless controls cannot make the run go on without end) next to the numbers. Named control: say why it skips the word test (the person named it on purpose) and why a missing one fails the capture instead of being skipped (a control the person asked for and the run could not click must be heard, not hidden).

criteria.evidence: "In: the file's path, and who gave it." "Given a web-page file, when it is captured, then the fingerprint of the copy equals one worked out from the original."

"saves an exact copy of one web-page file, and a picture and the text of each view." "The browser goes two clicks deep. It clicks each control on the first screen, then each new control those views add."
"In: any more pages to capture, and any named controls to click on the first page. Both are optional." "It follows relative links." "A person gives one web-page file"
criteria.fix: Say what a "more page" is and how it is handled. The page says a person gives one web-page file, lists "any more pages to capture" as an input, and says the browser follows relative links, but never says whether a more page is another file the person names, or a page reached by a relative link, nor how its views are counted (do they count toward the 40-view and 160-click limits?). Add one rule in Rules & behavior that states what a more page is, how it is captured, and how it counts. Also add the reasons named in the self_explanation fix, so a cold reader can explain why the run stops where it does.
